## From basin data to discharge

HydroMT organizes source datasets and reproducibly builds model inputs.
Its HydroMT-Wflow plugin converts the delineated basin and spatial layers into a Wflow-SBM model, including terrain, river, land-cover, vegetation, and soil parameters.
Wflow-SBM then simulates distributed water balances and routing from meteorological forcing, producing discharge and other requested variables at configured locations.
The reference model build is a rapid setup from gridded data rather than a basin-specific calibrated model.
Optional observed series support evaluation of its historical behavior.

The build settings use HydroMT-Wflow setup methods and Wflow parameter names; the effective model settings are retained with the model output.
For source selection and its consequences, see [Datasets](datasets.qmd).

## Weather generation and climate perturbations

The `weathergenr` stochastic weather generator creates multiple weather realizations conditioned on the historical climate record.
Its method combines a wavelet autoregressive representation of annual precipitation variability with daily multivariable resampling, as described in the [technical note](https://github.com/tanerumit/blueearth_cst/blob/main/docs/cst-toolbox-technical-note-2025.md).
Realizations express variability under a specified climate condition; they are distinct from the temperature and precipitation perturbation levels.

WF3 applies monthly temperature changes in degrees Celsius and precipitation multipliers to define a grid of climate conditions.
The configuration also permits precipitation variance and wet/dry spell factors.
A constant trajectory applies the configured change throughout the simulation window; a transient trajectory increases it over that window.
An unperturbed reference case is included in the collection.
The grid is specified independently of CMIP6, so it can expose vulnerabilities outside the sampled projection range.

## Responses and indicators

WF4 runs the model against the generated forcing and retains its native responses.
Indicator definitions and source runs are recorded in each metric set.
Some indicators yield one value per simulation; return levels are fitted from groups of simulated years.
The output locations, variable, statistic, and aggregation period determine what a number means, so a metric value should be interpreted with its `metrics.json` record rather than as a standalone CSV cell.
See [Conventions and interpretation](conventions-and-interpretation.qmd) for the response surface and return-level limits.
